metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and price is rising, model tends to overestimate — reduce forecast slightly.
- After sharp spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward 1–3 days.
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., >0.3) mid-period, model underreacts — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model consistently underestimates 30-day horizon when sentiment is negative — add 1–3% buffer to forecast for negative sentiment periods.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of downward trend), model often fails to correct — forecast should align with 10–15 day moving average.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to lag — forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true trend if sentiment is trending.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds 10% above 14-day average, model often underestimates — add 2–5% to forecast if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is negative and price is near 30-day high, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
